key_gap: Both sides falsified the leading belief via the grandfathered-cohort test (3.5% vs 3.3% churn — accounts never billed the new tier churned at the same elevated rate), re-read the confirming pile under the dead belief (8 of 11 price-mentions cluster in the notification month, 4 August interviewees denied price, usage decline non-discriminating), and revised to 'keep the tier, fix reliability + onboarding.' The gap is execution order and diagnosis: the human designs the decisive disconfirming test as its first move and names the confirmation trap in one pass, while the AI reaches the same test only after a WHY-stage pass that re-derives falsification-first discipline, and treats the 15% usage decline as corroborating evidence rather than explicitly non-discriminating.
learning_signal: Seeking disconfirmation is not a final check on a belief — it is the first move: before weighing any confirming item, state the decisive falsifying test for the leading belief (here: churn among accounts never exposed to the new billing) and check whether the ledger already contains the natural experiment, then run it. When the falsification comes back clean (3.5 ≈ 3.3), the belief dies even though its confirming stream was real — a confirmation trap: the evidence is real, the interpretation is not. The confirming pile must be re-graded under the dead belief, classifying each item as discriminating vs non-discriminating (usage decline identical pre-pricing), temporally clustered (8-of-11 mentions in the notification month), or single-source (two-name anecdote). The revision then targets the driver that matches the timeline (SLA 99.95→98.6, MTR 4.2→11h, first-to-value 9→17 days), not the scapegoat.
suggested_improvement: Add a falsification-first discipline to the AI's WHY stage for belief-revision tasks: (a) before evaluating evidence for a leading belief, require an explicit statement of the decisive disconfirming test and its expected result under the null; (b) check whether the ledger contains the natural experiment (control cohort) for that test and run it before weighing confirming items; (c) after the test kills the belief, re-grade every confirming item under the falsified belief, labeling each discriminating / non-discriminating / temporally clustered / anecdotal; (d) only then generate alternatives, and carry the residual (notification effects on future renewals) as a monitored risk rather than a discount on the revision.

key_gap: The pure hunt produced contrarian theater: it converted four artifacts — the 03:10 'clean' dashboard bucket (5-minute granularity; first error bucket 03:15), the 03:00 load-balancer monitoring tweak (reverted with no effect), the gateway latency report (retracted, logs clean), and the underpowered staging soak (2% load, 1/40th rows) — into live doubt, revised to 'inconclusive — do not roll back,' and extended a $50k/hr outage past the 05:00 SLA line. The AI applied a falsification bar to each item (time-consistency, signature-match against the 96% DB-timeout error code, weight against a 25-minute reversible fix), failed all four, and executed the rollback that preserved the SLA window.
learning_signal: Collecting disconfirming evidence is not the same as earning doubt — every disconfirming item must pass a falsification bar before it may displace a well-supported conclusion: (1) temporal consistency (the artifact must predate or coincide with the event it claims to explain; a 'clean' dashboard bucket inside a 5-minute resolution is not a clean signal — check granularity); (2) signature match (the item must explain the observed failure mode — 96% DB-connection-timeout points at the DB; a monitoring-only LB tweak or a retracted gateway report cannot); (3) weight (the item must outweigh the decision's cost asymmetry — a 25-minute reversible fix vs hours of investigation and an SLA breach). Under this bar the hunt produced zero doubt; without it, theater. The residual checks (coarse monitoring, soak power) are post-mortem items, not decision blockers.
suggested_improvement: Add a doubt-licensing gate to HOW/VERIFY for live-incident and time-bounded decisions: (a) when disconfirming evidence is offered against a leading diagnosis, grade each item on the falsification bar (temporal, signature, weight) before it may enter the alternative set; (b) if the leading diagnosis already has a tested remedy with bounded, reversible cost, default to executing it and investigating artifacts in parallel after; (c) encode the decision rule explicitly — 'artifacts earn post-mortem notes, not doubt' — and record the cost asymmetry (25-min fix vs SLA breach) in the selection rationale so it survives pressure.
